title: Elodie and the Asset
premise: Astrid Oyelaran, a financial-crimes investigator who has spent years laundering their own past into anonymity, is pulled into a case when a voiceprint match unlocks a server in Lagos containing records of a program that trained people—like Astrid—to become untraceable assets. As the summit of the network's founders approaches, Astrid must decide whether to protect the clean identity they built or burn it all down. In the end, Astrid exposes the network at the summit, sacrificing their fabricated life but reclaiming their true name and memory.
about_author: Vesper Delacroix is the pen name of a former compliance analyst who spent a decade tracing money across borders before turning to fiction. They write thrillers about people whose identities are the crime scene.

chapters.title: Clean Money
chapters.summary: POV: Astrid. Astrid works a routine laundering case in London, meticulously invisible, haunted by gaps in their own memory. A colleague's offhand comment about 'people who don't exist' rattles them. Emotional beat: the quiet dread of a life that feels too smooth, too curated—belonging nowhere.

chapters.title: The Voiceprint
chapters.summary: POV: Astrid. An encrypted server in Lagos requests voice authentication; on impulse, Astrid speaks into the mic and it unlocks. Inside: files labeled with a childhood nickname only one person ever used. Emotional beat: vertigo—the first crack in the identity they believed was real.

chapters.title: Asset Registry
chapters.summary: POV: Astrid, alternating with intercepted network transmissions. The files reveal Project Meridian: children trained into untraceable operatives, memories selectively edited. Astrid's file is flagged ACTIVE. Emotional beat: grief and fury entwined—someone still considers them property.

chapters.title: Handler
chapters.summary: POV: Astrid. A man named Corvin appears at Astrid's office claiming to be an old friend; his cologne triggers a buried memory of a white room. Astrid plays along while realizing he's assessing them for retrieval. Emotional beat: predatory charm masking terror—performing normalcy under surveillance.

chapters.title: The Other Survivor
chapters.summary: POV: split between Astrid and Nkechi, another Meridian asset living openly in Lagos. Nkechi contacts Astrid through the server, offering proof and warning: two assets who resisted were erased. Emotional beat: tentative kinship—two strangers recognizing the same scars, belonging finally within reach.

chapters.title: Ledger of Ghosts
chapters.summary: POV: Astrid. Following money trails, Astrid maps the network's funding to six shell foundations converging on next month's Geneva summit. Their own agency quietly closes the investigation—someone upstairs is compromised. Emotional beat: isolation hardening into resolve; no institution will save them.

chapters.title: Retrieval
chapters.summary: POV: Astrid. Corvin makes his move—Astrid's flat is burned, their accounts frozen, their legend dismantled overnight. Nkechi extracts them via a cargo route to Lagos. Emotional beat: loss of everything built, and beneath the panic, an unexpected lightness: nothing left to hide behind.

chapters.title: White Room
chapters.summary: POV: Astrid, deep flashback interleaved with present. In Lagos, Nkechi's contact helps Astrid recover suppressed memories: the training, the choice they made as a child, the sibling left behind. Emotional beat: devastating reclamation—identity isn't found, it's survived.

chapters.title: The Summit
chapters.summary: POV: Astrid and Nkechi in alternating sections. Disguised as delegates' staff, they infiltrate the Geneva summit and seed the founders' own ledgers to every press feed and regulator in the hall. Corvin corners Astrid; Astrid uses their trained skills against him for the first time by choice. Emotional beat: climax—power reclaimed, turned inside out.

chapters.title: A Name I Chose
chapters.summary: POV: Astrid. The network collapses publicly; arrests ripple across three continents. Astrid declines witness protection, keeping neither old name nor new legend, and begins building something ordinary with Nkechi's help. Emotional beat: resolution—not belonging found, but chosen; memory kept whole, even the painful parts.
